notes_for_us: The whole hook of this game is that the map is different every run — 'the storm changes the world', a new road opens and the old one closes, the village sometimes appears. Every field in the handoff describes a fixed map. There is no way to say 'these features are drawn from a pool' or 'this segment varies', so the emitted build is the union of all events at once, which is a different game.

Adventure has no vehicle-road row. `path-trail` says 'road' in its own text, so step 2 stops there, but it carries none of the width rules `path-road-vehicle` exists for — and this is a six-person truck on a mountain pass, where the road width is the game. Reaching options.md for one row on a 20 KB prompt is exactly the cost the skill warns about, so the width was lost.

The truck is the single most important object in the map and there is nowhere to put it. It is not an option, not a shape, and not `mechanics` — it is a piece of geometry the players ride in, and the only reason it appears in the build at all is that I wrote it into the road's text.

Two genres both wanted `hazard-kill` and `building-interior` with different sentences (Adventure's environmental danger vs Survival's shelter to hide in). The dedupe rule says the dominant genre's wording wins, but here the Survival sentence is the accurate one for the village — the rule is right about IDs and wrong about which sentence describes the thing.
